symbols.name: m
symbols.def: Number of decision times per unit.

symbols.name: ell
symbols.def: Index of the explicit bounded-aspect asymptotic experiment.

symbols.name: kappa
symbols.def: Exponent controlling the predeclared contrast family.

symbols.name: B
symbols.def: Uniform envelope for both potential outcomes.

symbols.name: Ccell
symbols.def: Cells carry row-major order: \( (i,j)\prec(i',j')\) when \(i<i'\), or when \(i=i'\) and \(j<j'\).

symbols.name: P
symbols.def: Law of the sequential randomized experiment and its proximal potential outcomes.

symbols.name: Ainit
symbols.def: Pre-experiment states \(A^{\mathrm{init}}=(A_{i0})_{i\in I}\), used only by the Markov witness and observed at global time zero.

symbols.name: Gglobal
symbols.def: The experiment filtration has \(\mathbb G_0\) equal to the recorded baseline field and, for \(k\ge1\), \(\mathbb G_k\) equal to the field after the assignment and outcome at the unique cell with row-major index \(k\) have been recorded.

symbols.name: F
symbols.def: Local notation is defined by \(\mathcal F_{i,0}=\mathbb G_{(i-1)m}\) and \(\mathcal F_{i,j}=\mathbb G_{o(i,j)}\) for \(j\in J\); every pre-cell conditional law is nevertheless taken with respect to \(\mathbb G_{o(i,j)-1}\).
symbols.role: Explicit row baselines and local history notation.

symbols.name: Sigma
symbols.def: Nonzero singular values in decreasing order in \(M=U\Sigma V^\top\).

symbols.name: L
symbols.def: Normalized maximum-row loss \(\mathcal L(\widetilde U,U)=\sqrt{n/(\mu r)}\min_{R\in\mathbb O_r}\lVert\widetilde U R-U\rVert_{2,\infty}\).

symbols.name: UhatI
symbols.def: Leading left singular vectors of \(\widehat M^{\mathrm I}\) under a fixed tie rule.

symbols.name: pbar
symbols.def: Marginal row propensities \(\bar p_i=m^{-1}\sum_{j\in J}E_P[p_{ij}]=m^{-1}\sum_{j\in J}E_P[A_{ij}]\).
symbols.role: Oracle expansion point for the blind denominator.

symbols.name: MB
symbols.def: Oracle blind center \(M^{\mathrm B}_{ij}=p_{ij}\mu^1_{ij}/\bar p_i-(1-p_{ij})\mu^0_{ij}/(1-\bar p_i)\).

symbols.name: Uoracle
symbols.def: Leading \(r\) left singular vectors \(U^{\mathrm O}\) of the oracle blind center \(M^{\mathrm B}\) under the fixed tie rule.

symbols.name: Dblind
symbols.def: Denominator tangent \(D^{\mathrm B}_{ij}=-(\widehat p_i-\bar p_i)H^{\mathrm B}_{ij}\).

symbols.name: Tblind
symbols.def: First-order blind target \(T^{\mathrm B}=M^{\mathrm B}+D^{\mathrm B}\).

symbols.name: Ublind
symbols.def: Leading \(r\) left singular vectors of \(T^{\mathrm B}\) under the fixed tie rule.

symbols.name: rho
symbols.def: Total restricted propensity drift \(\rho_{nm}=\mathcal L(U^{\mathrm B},U)\).

symbols.name: Zbar
symbols.def: Oracle-denominator blind score \(Z^{\bar p}_{ij}=A_{ij}Y_{ij}/\bar p_i-(1-A_{ij})Y_{ij}/(1-\bar p_i)\).
symbols.role: Martingale score centered at the oracle blind matrix.

symbols.name: Rblind
symbols.def: Centered-linear plus quadratic ratio residual \(R^{\mathrm B}=Z^{\mathrm B}-Z^{\bar p}-D^{\mathrm B}\).

symbols.name: MhatB
symbols.def: Blind rank \(r\) projection \(\widehat M^{\mathrm B}=\mathcal P_r(Z^{\mathrm B})\).

symbols.name: UhatB
symbols.def: Leading left singular vectors of \(\widehat M^{\mathrm B}\) under the fixed tie rule.

symbols.name: rhohat
symbols.def: Observable blind-versus-recorded discrepancy \(\widehat\rho_{nm}=\mathcal L(\widehat U^{\mathrm B},\widehat U^{\mathrm I})\).

symbols.name: gprime
symbols.def: Second generic dense loading matrix \(g'\), used for covariance entries.

symbols.name: Omega
symbols.def: The entry indexed by \(g,g'\in\mathcal G_n\) is \(\Omega_{gg'}=(s_gs_{g'})^{-1}\sum_{i,j}E_P[g_{ij}g'_{ij}E_{ij}^2]\).

symbols.name: Omegap
symbols.def: The entry indexed by \(g,g'\in\mathcal G_n\) is \(\Omega^{\mathrm P}_{gg'}=(s_gs_{g'})^{-1}\sum_{i,j}g_{ij}g'_{ij}E_P[E_{ij}^2\mid\mathbb G_{o(i,j)-1}]\).

symbols.name: Mloo
symbols.role: Cross-fitted mean prediction without the target score.

symbols.name: shat
symbols.def: Leave-one-cell-out residual scales \(\widehat s_g^2=\sum_{i\in I,j\in J}g_{ij}^2\widehat e_{ij}^2\).

symbols.name: c
symbols.def: Conditional \(1-\alpha\) quantile \(c_{1-\alpha}\) of the standardized Gaussian multiplier maximum over \(\mathcal G_n\).

symbols.name: theta
symbols.def: Effect amplitude in the Markov witness.

symbols.name: h
symbols.def: Common-arm amplitude in the Markov witness.

symbols.name: uD
symbols.def: Independent unit factors \(u^{\mathrm D}_i\sim\operatorname{Uniform}(0,1)\), which are almost surely distinct.

symbols.name: vD
symbols.def: Independent time factors \(v^{\mathrm D}_j\sim\operatorname{Uniform}(0,1)\), independent of \(u^{\mathrm D}\), which are almost surely distinct.

symbols.name: MD
symbols.def: Comparator effect matrix \(M^{\mathrm D}_{ij}=f^{\mathrm D}_1(u^{\mathrm D}_i,v^{\mathrm D}_j)-f^{\mathrm D}_0(u^{\mathrm D}_i,v^{\mathrm D}_j)=\exp(u^{\mathrm D}_iv^{\mathrm D}_j)\).

symbols.name: W
symbols.def: The explicit bounded-aspect sequence of \(0.25/0.75\) Markov-mask laws in \(\mathrm{def:markov\mbox{-}witness}\).

symbols.name: Eobs
symbols.def: Class \(\mathfrak E_{n,m}=\{\widetilde U:\widetilde U\text{ is }\mathcal O_{n,m}\text{-measurable and takes values in }\mathbb O_{n,r}\}\).

symbols.name: Cstar
symbols.def: Asymptotic minimax constant along \((n_\ell,m_\ell)\), as constructed in \(\mathrm{def:sharp\mbox{-}experiment}\).

symbols.name: H
symbols.def: Filtration-preserving row deletion, matrix martingale concentration, local row packings, and sequential likelihood conditioning.
symbols.role: Starting move for the sharp-constant question.

assumptions.condition: For every \(i\in I\) and \(j\in J\), \(P(A_{ij}=1\mid\mathbb G_{o(i,j)-1},Y_{ij}(0),Y_{ij}(1))=p_{ij}\) almost surely.
For every \(i\in I\) and \(j\in J\), \(q\le p_{ij}\le1-q\) almost surely.
For every \(i\in I\), \(j\in J\), and \(a\in\{0,1\}\), \(|Y_{ij}(a)|\le B\) almost surely.
The effect matrix satisfies \(\operatorname{rank}(M)=r\).
The left singular space satisfies \(\lVert U\rVert_{2,\infty}\le\sqrt{\mu r/n}\).
The right singular space satisfies \(\lVert V\rVert_{2,\infty}\le\sqrt{\mu r/m}\).
The signal condition number satisfies \(\sigma_1(M)/\sigma_r(M)\le K\).
The smallest nonzero singular value satisfies \(\sigma_r(M)\ge\lambda_{nm}\).
The dimensions satisfy \(c_-\le m/n\le c_+\) for fixed \(0<c_-<c_+<\infty\).
The predictable propensity path satisfies \(\max_{i\in I}|m^{-1}\sum_{j\in J}(p_{ij}-E_P[p_{ij}])|=O_P(\sqrt{\log(en)/m})\).

novel.justification: This law-level stability condition holds for deterministic schedules and for bounded finite-state geometrically ergodic personalization rules, including the exhibited two-state Markov witness; it excludes persistent random policy regimes for which a single empirical row fraction has no stable design target.

assumptions.condition: The primitive oracle blind center satisfies \(\sigma_r(M^{\mathrm B})-\sigma_{r+1}(M^{\mathrm B})\ge c_{\mathrm B}\lambda_{nm}\) almost surely for a fixed \(c_{\mathrm B}>0\), with \(\sigma_{r+1}(M^{\mathrm B})=0\) when \(r=\min(n,m)\).

novel.justification: This is a law-level separation condition on the oracle pseudo-outcome before empirical normalization. It is directly checkable for deterministic schedules, block-randomized designs, and the displayed Markov law, where the two oracle singular values are explicit; it does not impose any property on the realized row denominator or on a fitted matrix.

assumptions.condition: The family satisfies \(2\le|\mathcal G_n|\le n^{\kappa}\).
Every \(g\in\mathcal G_n\) satisfies \(c_g/(nm)\le\lVert g\rVert_{\mathrm F}^2\le C_g/(nm)\).

novel.justification: Grand means, time-window means, and subgroup-by-window means encoded with deterministic weights have squared Frobenius norm of order \(1/(nm)\); the two-sided scale restriction keeps the causal queries nonvanishing without referring to an estimated singular space.

assumptions.condition: Every \(g\in\mathcal G_n\) satisfies \(\max_{i\in I,j\in J}|g_{ij}|\le C_\infty/(nm)\).

novel.justification: Predeclared averages over a fixed positive fraction of unit-time cells have entry weights of order \(1/(nm)\). This excludes localized entry queries, for which a dense-average central limit theorem is not the relevant inferential object.

assumptions.condition: For every \(g\in\mathcal G_n\), \(s_g^2=\sum_{i\in I,j\in J}E_P[g_{ij}^2E_{ij}^2]\ge c_sB^2/(nm)\).
The normalized predictable covariance satisfies \(E_P[\lVert\Omega^{\mathrm P}_{nm}-\Omega_{nm}\rVert_{\max}]\le (nm)^{-1/16}/\log^2(enm|\mathcal G_n|)\).
With probability at least \(1-(nm)^{-1/16}\), \(\Omega^{\mathrm P}_{nm}\preceq[1+(nm)^{-1/16}/\log^2|\mathcal G_n|]\Omega_{nm}\).
With probability at least \(1-(nm)^{-1/16}\), \(\lVert\Omega^{\mathrm P}_{nm}-\Omega_{nm}\rVert_{\max}\le(nm)^{-1/16}/\log^2(enm|\mathcal G_n|)\).
The inference branch satisfies \(r<\min(n,m)\).

novel.justification: Nonsaturated effect surfaces are natural in long mobile-health panels with a small latent response dimension. This restriction is imposed only for feasible variance estimation, because a saturated rank interpolates every score and makes residual studentization identically zero.

assumptions.condition: The inference branch satisfies \((nm)^{1/8}r(n+m)\log^6(enm)/(nmq)+(nm)^{1/8}B^2(n+m)\log^4(enm)/(q\lambda_{nm}^2)=o(1)\).

novel.justification: This primitive effective-dimension and signal margin permits fixed or slowly growing rank with singular values above the adaptive score-noise scale in bounded-aspect longitudinal panels. It makes aggregate leave-one-cell-out prediction error negligible for dense averages without assuming residual consistency itself.

definitions.name: Row-major global experiment filtration
definitions.construction: Order \(\mathcal C_{n,m}=I\times J\) by \(o(i,j)=(i-1)m+j\). Let \(\mathbb G_0\) be the recorded baseline field and let \(\mathbb G_k\) be the field after recording the assignment and outcome at the unique cell \(o^{-1}(k)\), together with all earlier cells. Define \(\mathcal F_{i,0}=\mathbb G_{(i-1)m}\) and \(\mathcal F_{i,j}=\mathbb G_{o(i,j)}\) for \(j\in J\).
inputs: The row and time indices and the recorded cell sequence.

definitions.name: Predictable low-rank experiment class
definitions.construction: \(\mathfrak P^{\mathrm{pred}}_{n,m}(r,\mu,K,q,B,\lambda)=\{P\in\mathcal P_{n,m}:\text{ assumptions }\mathrm{ass:sequential\mbox{-}randomization},\mathrm{ass:overlap},\mathrm{ass:bounded\mbox{-}outcomes},\mathrm{ass:exact\mbox{-}rank},\mathrm{ass:left\mbox{-}incoherence},\mathrm{ass:right\mbox{-}incoherence},\mathrm{ass:condition\mbox{-}number},\mathrm{ass:signal\mbox{-}floor},\mathrm{ass:aspect\mbox{-}ratio}\text{ hold for the }(n,m)\text{ array}\}\).

definitions.name: Normalized maximum-row loss
definitions.construction: \(\mathcal L(\widetilde U,U)=\sqrt{n/(\mu r)}\min_{R\in\mathbb O_r}\lVert\widetilde U R-U\rVert_{2,\infty}\).
inputs: A candidate and target row-factor matrix.

definitions.name: Recorded-propensity IPW score
definitions.construction: Set \(Z^{\mathrm{ipw}}_{ij}=A_{ij}Y_{ij}/p_{ij}-(1-A_{ij})Y_{ij}/(1-p_{ij})\) and \(E_{ij}=Z^{\mathrm{ipw}}_{ij}-M_{ij}\) for every \(i\in I\) and \(j\in J\).

definitions.name: Recorded-propensity IPW-SVD
definitions.construction: Compute \(\widehat M^{\mathrm I}=\mathcal P_r(Z^{\mathrm{ipw}})\) and report its leading left singular matrix \(\widehat U^{\mathrm I}\) under the fixed tie rule.

definitions.name: Corrected maximum-row frontier
inputs: The geometric term, outcome scale, signal floor, and row cardinality.

definitions.name: Blind ratio target and total drift
definitions.construction: Set \(\bar p_i=m^{-1}\sum_{j\in J}E_P[p_{ij}]=m^{-1}\sum_{j\in J}E_P[A_{ij}]\), \(\widehat p_i=\Pi_{[q/2,1-q/2]}(m^{-1}\sum_{j\in J}A_{ij})\), \(M^{\mathrm B}_{ij}=p_{ij}\mu^1_{ij}/\bar p_i-(1-p_{ij})\mu^0_{ij}/(1-\bar p_i)\), \(H^{\mathrm B}_{ij}=p_{ij}\mu^1_{ij}/\bar p_i^2+(1-p_{ij})\mu^0_{ij}/(1-\bar p_i)^2\), \(D^{\mathrm B}_{ij}=-(\widehat p_i-\bar p_i)H^{\mathrm B}_{ij}\), and \(T^{\mathrm B}=M^{\mathrm B}+D^{\mathrm B}\). Let \(U^{\mathrm O}\) and \(U^{\mathrm B}\) be the leading \(r\) left singular matrices of \(M^{\mathrm B}\) and \(T^{\mathrm B}\), respectively, under the fixed tie rule, and set \(\rho_{nm}=\mathcal L(U^{\mathrm B},U)\).
inputs: The law, propensity path, assignments, and conditional arm means.

definitions.name: Blind row-scaled SVD
definitions.construction: Set \(Z^{\mathrm B}_{ij}=A_{ij}Y_{ij}/\widehat p_i-(1-A_{ij})Y_{ij}/(1-\widehat p_i)\), compute \(\widehat M^{\mathrm B}=\mathcal P_r(Z^{\mathrm B})\), and report its leading left singular matrix \(\widehat U^{\mathrm B}\).
inputs: Assignments and outcomes, discarding entrywise propensities.

definitions.name: Observable blind-versus-recorded diagnostic
definitions.construction: Compute both row-factor fits and set \(\widehat\rho_{nm}=\mathcal L(\widehat U^{\mathrm B},\widehat U^{\mathrm I})\).
inputs: The blind and recorded-propensity row-factor fits.

definitions.name: Blind ratio expansion residual
definitions.construction: Set \(Z^{\bar p}_{ij}=A_{ij}Y_{ij}/\bar p_i-(1-A_{ij})Y_{ij}/(1-\bar p_i)\) and \(R^{\mathrm B}=Z^{\mathrm B}-Z^{\bar p}-D^{\mathrm B}\).
inputs: The oracle row propensity and the realized blind score.

definitions.name: Leave-one-cell-out direct IPW multiplier process
definitions.construction: For every cell \( (i,j)\), replace only \(Z^{\mathrm{ipw}}_{ij}\) by zero, compute \(\widehat M^{(-ij)}=\mathcal P_r(Z^{\mathrm{ipw}}-Z^{\mathrm{ipw}}_{ij}e_ie_j^\top)\), and set \(\widehat e_{ij}=Z^{\mathrm{ipw}}_{ij}-\widehat M^{(-ij)}_{ij}\). For every \(g\in\mathcal G_n\), set \(\widehat\tau_g=\sum_{i,j}g_{ij}Z^{\mathrm{ipw}}_{ij}\) and \(\widehat s_g^2=\sum_{i,j}g_{ij}^2\widehat e_{ij}^2\). Draw conditionally independent \(\xi_{ij}\sim N(0,1)\), and define \(c_{1-\alpha}\) as the conditional \(1-\alpha\) quantile of \(\max_{g\in\mathcal G_n}|\sum_{i,j}\xi_{ij}g_{ij}\widehat e_{ij}/\widehat s_g|\).
inputs: The IPW score, rank, and deterministic contrast family.

definitions.name: Rank-one \(0.25/0.75\) Markov-mask witness
definitions.construction: Along \(n_\ell=2\ell\) and \(m_\ell=2\lceil\gamma\ell\rceil\), define \(W^{\theta,h}_\ell\) using independent baseline states \(A^{\mathrm{init}}_i=A_{i0}\sim\operatorname{Bernoulli}(1/2)\), recorded in \(\mathbb G_0\), and fixed \(0<\theta<h\) with \(h+\theta/2\le B\). For \(j\ge1\), set \(p_{ij}=1/2+(1/4)(-1)^{i+j}(2A_{i,j-1}-1)\), \(C_{ij}=h(-1)^{i+j}(2A_{i,j-1}-1)\), \(Y_{ij}(1)=\mu^1_{ij}=C_{ij}+(\theta/2)(-1)^{i+j}\), and \(Y_{ij}(0)=\mu^0_{ij}=C_{ij}-(\theta/2)(-1)^{i+j}\), where \(A_{i,j-1}=A^{\mathrm{init}}_i\) at \(j=1\). Hence \(M_{ij}=\theta(-1)^{i+j}\), \(\bar p_i=1/2\), and \(M^{\mathrm B}_{ij}=h+\theta(-1)^{i+j}\).
inputs: The explicit bounded-aspect path and amplitudes \(0<\theta<h\) bounded by \(B\).

definitions.name: Nonlinear-factor separation witness
definitions.construction: Draw independent \(u^{\mathrm D}_i,v^{\mathrm D}_j\sim\operatorname{Uniform}(0,1)\), set \(f^{\mathrm D}_0(u,v)=0\) and \(f^{\mathrm D}_1(u,v)=\exp(uv)\), and form \(M^{\mathrm D}_{ij}=\exp(u^{\mathrm D}_iv^{\mathrm D}_j)\).
inputs: Independent unit and time factors on a compact positive interval.

definitions.name: Observed-experiment estimator class
definitions.construction: Set \(\mathcal O_{n,m}=\sigma(A,Y,p)\) and \(\mathfrak E_{n,m}=\{\widetilde U:\widetilde U\text{ is }\mathcal O_{n,m}\text{-measurable and }\widetilde U\in\mathbb O_{n,r}\}\).
inputs: The observed assignments, outcomes, and recorded propensities.

definitions.name: Bounded-aspect sharp-constant experiment
definitions.construction: Fix \(\gamma\in(c_-,c_+)\), set \(n_\ell=2\ell\) and \(m_\ell=2\lceil\gamma\ell\rceil\), and define \(C_\star=\liminf_{\ell\to\infty}\inf_{\widetilde U\in\mathfrak E_{n_\ell,m_\ell}}\sup_{P\in\mathfrak P^{\mathrm{pred}}_{n_\ell,m_\ell}(r,\mu,K,q,B,\lambda)}E_P[\mathcal L(\widetilde U,U)]/b_{n_\ell m_\ell}\).
inputs: A fixed aspect limit and the predictable experiment class.

definitions.name: Sharp-frontier handle
definitions.construction: Use row deletion that preserves the global filtration to derive the rowwise martingale influence array, embed separated row-sign alternatives in the constant-propensity submodel, and compare local risks by sequential likelihood conditioning.
inputs: The upper expansion and constant-propensity packing.

statements.statement: For every \(i\in I\) and \(j\in J\), \(E_P[Z^{\mathrm{ipw}}_{ij}\mid\mathbb G_{o(i,j)-1}]=M_{ij}\). Hence the row-major sequence \((E_{o^{-1}(k)},\mathbb G_k)_{k=1}^{nm}\) is a matrix martingale-difference array, with conditional variance bounded by a constant times \(B^2/q\) and increment magnitude bounded by a constant times \(B/q\).
statements.justification: This identifies the effect matrix and exposes the conditional variance and increment scales needed by rowwise perturbation.
statements.gap: Hadad et al. identify scalar adaptive IPW scores, not their rowwise spectral use.
statements.consumer: It supplies a correctly scaled effect surface for micro-randomized trials with saved propensities.

statements.statement: Let \(p_{ij}=q_0\in(q,1-q)\), \(n/m\to c_0\in(0,\infty)\), and \(r=\mu=K=1\). If \(\lambda_{nm}\asymp B\sqrt{n\log n}\), then \(b_{nm}\asymp1\), and bounded nonzero common arm means give \(\sqrt n\lVert EV/\sigma_1(M)\rVert_\infty=\Omega_P(1)\). If \(\lambda_{nm}\asymp B\sqrt{nm}\), then \(b_{nm}\asymp\sqrt{\log n/n}\), the independent full-matrix maximum-row scale. Also \(Z^{\mathrm B}=Z^{\mathrm{ipw}}+D^{\mathrm B}+R^{\mathrm B}\), with \(D^{\mathrm B}_{ij}=-(\widehat p_i-q_0)[\mu^1_{ij}/q_0+\mu^0_{ij}/(1-q_0)]\); this is generally first order, and it vanishes only when the displayed derivative loading is zero.
statements.justification: This pins down the signal regimes and shows why empirical row normalization has its own first-order tangent.
statements.gap: Mehrotra et al.'s public Algorithm 1 gives the independent-assignment empirical-row-scaling benchmark for separate arm fits; the signed recorded-score decomposition here isolates the denominator tangent relevant to the new blind procedure.
statements.consumer: Analysts can distinguish a fixed known denominator from a random row-total normalization.

statements.statement: Fix \(q<1/4\) and the amplitudes in \(\mathrm{def:markov\mbox{-}witness}\). For all sufficiently large \(\ell\), the bounded Markov law \(W_\ell\) lies in \(\mathfrak P^{\mathrm{pred}}_{n_\ell,m_\ell}(1,1,1,q,B,\theta\sqrt{n_\ell m_\ell})\), but its arm means depend on \(A_{i,j-1}\), so it is not generated by the exogenous unit and time factors in Dwivedi et al.'s published equation (4) on page 2383. Conversely, their published Assumption 6 on page 2397 and Theorem 4.1 on page 2398 contain the bounded Lipschitz nonlinear-factor law generated by \(f^{\mathrm D}_0\), \(f^{\mathrm D}_1\), \(u^{\mathrm D}\), and \(v^{\mathrm D}\), for which \(\operatorname{rank}(M^{\mathrm D})=\min(n,m)\) almost surely; this law is excluded by \(\operatorname{rank}(M)=r\) for fixed \(r\). Thus their unit-by-time nearest-neighbor bound in published Theorem 3.1 and equations (17)--(18) on page 2389 and the normalized maximum-row IPW-SVD frontier are non-representable in either direction.
statements.justification: This gives the exact model-theoretic separation from the closest adaptive pooled unit-by-time factor result.
statements.gap: Dwivedi et al., published Theorem 3.1 and equations (17)--(18) on page 2389, control a nearest-neighbor unit-by-time arm-mean error under the factor structure in equation (4) on page 2383, not a row-subspace loss under treatment-path-dependent arm means.
statements.consumer: Referees can distinguish the row-factor target and predictable-mask domain from published adaptive counterfactual imputation.

statements.statement: Uniformly over \(P\in\mathfrak P^{\mathrm{pred}}_{n,m}(r,\mu,K,q,B,\lambda)\) in regimes with \(b_{nm}=o(1)\), recorded-propensity IPW-SVD satisfies \(\mathcal L(\widehat U^{\mathrm I},U)=O_P(b_{nm})\). This maximum-row claim is pointwise in the target and contains no factor depending on \(|\mathcal G_n|\).
statements.justification: This is the calibrated martingale maximum-row recovery theorem.
statements.gap: Mehrotra et al., public Algorithm 1, Theorem 3.2, and Corollary 3.3 in Section 3, attain the same geometric rowwise matrix-error scale using armwise empirical-row-scaled SVD under independent Bernoulli assignments, unknown propensities, and low-rankness of each arm mean. That result neither permits history-predictable assignments nor studies the left singular space of an effect matrix when the two arm means themselves may be high rank. Cai et al., published Assumptions 1--2 on page 948 and Theorem 1, equations (16b)--(17) on page 950, require independent Bernoulli entries and independent noise for a diagonal-deleted Gram estimator. Han et al., published equation (1) on page 1964 and Theorem 2.2 on page 1974, prove a Frobenius-rate online SGD result for independent Gaussian matrix contexts. Athey et al., published Assumptions 1--2 and Theorem 2, equation (14), on pages 1720 and 1724, and Sun et al., published equation (1), Assumptions 1--3, equation (11), and Theorem 3 in Sections 2--4 of article e70002, control outcome-matrix Frobenius errors rather than predictable causal-effect row-subspace loss.
statements.consumer: HeartSteps II analysts can recover latent response profiles without treating personalized probabilities as independent.

statements.statement: For fixed \(r\), \(\mu\), and \(K\), positive constants exist such that, whenever \(b_{nm}\) is below one fixed constant and \(\lambda_{nm}\le c_1B\sqrt{nm}\), \(\inf_{\widetilde U\in\mathfrak E_{n,m}}\sup_{P\in\mathfrak P^{\mathrm{pred}}_{n,m}(r,\mu,K,q,B,\lambda)}E_P[\mathcal L(\widetilde U,U)]\ge c_2b_{nm}\). The infimum is thus restricted to estimators measurable with respect to \(\mathcal O_{n,m}=\sigma(A,Y,p)\), and the bound already holds on a constant-propensity submodel \(p_{ij}=q_0\in[q,1-q]\).
statements.justification: The converse tests whether the corrected adaptive scale is information-limited.
statements.gap: Cai et al., published Theorem 2 and equation (22b) on page 953, give a two-to-infinity lower bound for independent Gaussian noise observed through independent Bernoulli sampling; arXiv v5 page 10 corroborates the locator. Mehrotra et al.'s public Theorem 3.2 and Corollary 3.3, Athey et al.'s published Theorem 2, equation (14), on page 1724, and Sun et al.'s published Theorem 3 in Section 4 of article e70002 are upper-error results and contain no normalized effect-subspace minimax experiment. The present converse instead embeds a bounded causal score with observed propensities and permits predictable masks; Wang et al. study Frobenius risk under fixed heterogeneous sampling.
statements.consumer: Trial designers obtain a lower benchmark linking decision budget, outcome scale, and signal strength.

statements.statement: Under sequential randomization, overlap, bounded outcomes, bounded aspect ratio, propensity-path stability, and \(b_{nm}=o(1)\), \(\max_{i\in I}|\widehat p_i-\bar p_i|=O_P(\sqrt{\log(en)/m})\) and \(\lVert D^{\mathrm B}\rVert/\lambda_{nm}=O_P(Bq^{-2}\sqrt{n\log(en)}/\lambda_{nm})=O_P(b_{nm})=o_P(1)\). If the primitive oracle gap holds, then \(P\{\sigma_r(T^{\mathrm B})-\sigma_{r+1}(T^{\mathrm B})\ge(c_{\mathrm B}/2)\lambda_{nm}\}\to1\).
statements.justification: This derives the realized tangent gap from a primitive oracle gap and path concentration instead of assuming a property of the random normalized target.
statements.gap: Cai et al. perturb a fixed signal under independent entries, while Khan and Ugander linearize scalar ratios; neither transfers an oracle singular gap through a same-path adaptive row denominator.
statements.consumer: It supplies a checkable sufficient condition for stable blind SVD in archived experiments.

statements.statement: Under overlap, bounded outcomes, bounded aspect ratio, propensity-path stability, the primitive oracle gap, and \(b_{nm}=o(1)\), \(Z^{\mathrm B}=Z^{\bar p}+D^{\mathrm B}+R^{\mathrm B}\), where \(E_P[Z^{\bar p}_{ij}\mid\mathbb G_{o(i,j)-1}]=M^{\mathrm B}_{ij}\). The residual \(R^{\mathrm B}\), which contains the centered linear derivative and the quadratic ratio term, contributes \(o_P(b_{nm})\) to normalized maximum-row subspace loss, and \(\mathcal L(\widehat U^{\mathrm B},U^{\mathrm B})=O_P(b_{nm})\).
statements.justification: This exhibits the empirical denominator as a leading object rather than hiding it in a remainder.
statements.gap: Khan and Ugander's published Theorem 3 and equation (10) on page 7 analyze a scalar affine normalizer under independent treatment indicators, not a same-path row ratio inside an SVD; their Discussion on page 18 lists dependent indicators as an open extension.
statements.consumer: It audits legacy mobile-health data retaining treatment counts but not decision probabilities.

statements.statement: Uniformly over sequences in the predictable class satisfying propensity-path stability, the primitive oracle gap, and \(b_{nm}=o(1)\), \(\bigl|\mathcal L(\widehat U^{\mathrm B},U)-\rho_{nm}\bigr|=O_P(b_{nm})\) and the observed discrepancy satisfies \(\bigl|\widehat\rho_{nm}-\rho_{nm}\bigr|=O_P(b_{nm})\). Therefore \(\mathcal L(\widehat U^{\mathrm B},U)=O_P(b_{nm})\) if and only if \(\rho_{nm}=O_P(b_{nm})\), if and only if \(\widehat\rho_{nm}=O_P(b_{nm})\). Thus \(\widehat\rho_{nm}\) is an observable rate certificate: tightness of \(\widehat\rho_{nm}/b_{nm}\) certifies frontier-rate validity, whereas \(\widehat\rho_{nm}/b_{nm}\to\infty\) certifies its failure.
statements.justification: The theorem turns the latent total-drift boundary into an observed comparison of two fitted row spaces.
statements.gap: Khan and Ugander's scalar affine normalizer does not provide an observed spectral diagnostic for a row-fraction SVD.
statements.consumer: A data steward can compare the two reported fits and decide whether discarding saved personalization probabilities preserves the rowwise frontier.

statements.statement: Fix \(\gamma\in(c_-,c_+)\), \(q<1/4\), \(r=1\), \(\mu=K=1\), and \(0<\theta<h\) with \(h+\theta/2\le B\). Along \(n_\ell=2\ell\) and \(m_\ell=2\lceil\gamma\ell\rceil\), for all sufficiently large \(\ell\) the law \(W_\ell\) belongs to \(\mathfrak P^{\mathrm{pred}}_{n_\ell,m_\ell}(1,1,1,q,B,\theta\sqrt{n_\ell m_\ell})\), satisfies propensity-path stability, and satisfies the primitive oracle gap with \(c_{\mathrm B}=(h-\theta)/\theta\). It has \(b_{n_\ell m_\ell}\asymp\sqrt{\log n_\ell/n_\ell}\). Its marginal row propensity is \(\bar p_i=1/2\), and Markov concentration gives \(\max_i|\widehat p_i-1/2|=O_P(\sqrt{\log n_\ell/m_\ell})\). Consequently \(T^{\mathrm B}=h\mathbf1_{n_\ell}\mathbf1_{m_\ell}^\top+\theta((-1)^{i+j})_{ij}+o_P(\sqrt{n_\ell m_\ell})\) in operator norm, so \(\rho_{n_\ell m_\ell}\to2\), \(\widehat\rho_{n_\ell m_\ell}\to2\), \(\mathcal L(\widehat U^{\mathrm I},U)=O_P(b_{n_\ell m_\ell})\), and \(\mathcal L(\widehat U^{\mathrm B},U)\to2\). This is a boundary example for \(\mathrm{def:blind\mbox{-}svd}\), not a claim about any published normalization procedure.
statements.justification: This explicit calculation is the early kill test and a boundary example for the newly introduced row-fraction procedure.
statements.gap: Mehrotra et al.'s public Algorithm 1 also uses empirical row fractions, but it fits the two arm-mean matrices separately under independent assignments; the signed-score procedure in \(\mathrm{def:blind\mbox{-}svd}\) is different, and the predictable Markov witness violates their assignment model. The proposition is therefore a boundary example for the procedure defined here, not a refutation of their theorem or any other published procedure.
statements.consumer: HeartSteps-style simulations obtain a fully specified stress design using probabilities \(0.25\) and \(0.75\), with an observed discrepancy that detects failure.

statements.statement: Let \(N=nm\), \(d=|\mathcal G_n|\), and order cells by \(o\). Under the inference assumptions, \((X_{k,g},\mathbb G_k)_{k=1}^N\) is a \(d\)-dimensional martingale-difference array, \(N^{-1}\sum_{k=1}^NE_P[\lVert X_k\rVert_\infty^3]=O(1)\le N^{1/8}\), and polynomial family growth implies \(\log^{7/2}d=o(N^{1/4})\), which is Belloni and Oliveira's growth inequality with \(\delta_N=N^{-1/16}\) and \(\varrho=1/8\). Matrix Freedman concentration gives \(\max_{g,g'}|N^{-1}\sum_{k=1}^N\{X_{k,g}X_{k,g'}-E_P[X_{k,g}X_{k,g'}\mid\mathbb G_{k-1}]\}|=o_P(N^{-1/8}\log^{-2}(eNd))\). Deterministic leave-one-cell-out rank \(r\) approximation then gives \(\max_{g,g'\in\mathcal G_n}|(s_gs_{g'})^{-1}\sum_{i,j}g_{ij}g'_{ij}\widehat e_{ij}^2-\Omega_{gg'}|=o_P(\log^{-2}(enm d))\) and \(N^{-1}\max_{g\in\mathcal G_n}\sum_{k=1}^N(\widehat X_{k,g}-X_{k,g})^2=o_P(N^{-1/8}\log^{-2}(eNd))\). Consequently \(\max_g|\widehat s_g/s_g-1|=o_P(\log^{-2}(eNd))\) and \(P(\min_g\widehat s_g\ge\tfrac12\sqrt{c_s}B/\sqrt{N})\to1\). These conclusions use no independence claim for the leave-one-cell-out fits.
statements.justification: This discharges the increment, dimension-growth, empirical-covariance, residual-consistency, and positive-studentizer obligations instead of assuming feasible bootstrap validity.
statements.gap: Belloni and Oliveira's Assumption 2 and Theorem 3.3 begin with normalized martingale increments and a plug-in increment approximation; they do not derive those objects from adaptive low-rank causal scores.
statements.consumer: It provides a checkable audit trail for simultaneous HeartSteps II contrasts and prevents saturated-rank residual collapse.

statements.statement: Uniformly over \(P\in\mathfrak P^{\mathrm{pred}}_{n,m}(r,\mu,K,q,B,\lambda)\), only the inference branch additionally requires \(r<\min(n,m)\), the low-rank growth margin, deterministic polynomial-size dense average-scale loadings, variance nondegeneracy, and Belloni--Oliveira predictable-covariance stabilization. Under these conditions, the conditional leave-one-cell-out multiplier law consistently approximates \(\max_{g\in\mathcal G_n}|(\widehat\tau_g-\tau_g)/\widehat s_g|\). Thus \(P(\tau_g\in[\widehat\tau_g\pm c_{1-\alpha}\widehat s_g]\text{ for every }g\in\mathcal G_n)\to1-\alpha\). Pointwise radii obey \(\widehat s_g=O_P(B/\sqrt{nmq})\), while \(c_{1-\alpha}=O_P(\sqrt{\log|\mathcal G_n|})\); this query-family multiplier is not part of \(b_{nm}\), and no rank restriction is added to Theorems 2--4.
statements.justification: The result separates query multiplicity from row-factor recovery.
statements.gap: Belloni and Oliveira's arXiv Assumption 2 on pages 7--8 and Theorem 3.3 on page 8 give a generic martingale multiplier theorem after normalized increments and plug-in consistency are supplied. The lemma here derives those hypotheses for deterministic dense causal loadings and leave-one-cell-out low-rank residuals. Xia and Yuan's loading-alignment conditions are not used. Ma et al.'s published Theorem 4 and equation (14) on page 348 concern a coefficient matrix under modeled nonadaptive missingness.
statements.consumer: HeartSteps II investigators can report familywise-valid proximal-effect averages.

statements.statement: Along the explicit path \(n_\ell=2\ell\) and \(m_\ell=2\lceil\gamma\ell\rceil\), determine \(C_\star\), decide whether recorded IPW-SVD attains it among \(\mathcal O_{n_\ell,m_\ell}\)-measurable estimators, and characterize whether a nonconstant predictable propensity path can be least favorable.
statements.justification: Rate matching does not determine the local information geometry.
statements.gap: No cited adaptive low-rank result computes this maximum-row minimax constant.
statements.consumer: The answer determines whether personalization can be optimized for inferential efficiency.

sampling_model.design: A triangular array of sequential randomized decisions ordered globally by \(o(i,j)=(i-1)m+j\), with filtration \((\mathbb G_k)_{k=0}^{nm}\) and explicit row baselines \(\mathcal F_{i,0}=\mathbb G_{(i-1)m}\).
sampling_model.units: \(n\) units observed at \(m\) ordered decision times, with bounded aspect ratio; the sharp experiment and Markov witness use \(n_\ell=2\ell\) and \(m_\ell=2\lceil\gamma\ell\rceil\).
sampling_model.treatment: Binary \(A_{ij}\) is drawn with \(p_{ij}\in[q,1-q]\) given the global pre-cell field \(\mathbb G_{o(i,j)-1}\).
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: Recorded IPW-SVD uses known propensities. The newly defined blind procedure uses a clipped row fraction; its tangent gap is derived from the primitive oracle gap and propensity-path stability and is included in \(\rho_{nm}\). The observable discrepancy \(\widehat\rho_{nm}\) compares blind and recorded fits and diagnoses frontier-rate validity. Only the simultaneous-inference branch assumes nonsaturated rank and effective-dimension growth; it uses leave-one-cell-out rank \(r\) residuals whose uniform covariance consistency and positive studentizers are derived rather than assumed.

estimand_functional: \(M_{ij}=E_P[Z^{\mathrm{ipw}}_{ij}\mid\mathbb G_{o(i,j)-1}],\quad\widehat U^{\mathrm I}=\operatorname{left}_r(\mathcal P_r(Z^{\mathrm{ipw}})),\quad\mathcal L(\widehat U^{\mathrm I},U)=O_P(b_{nm})\)

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Published Theorem 1, equations (16b)--(17) on page 950, gives the rowwise upper bound, and Theorem 2, equation (22b) on page 953, gives the minimax lower bound under independent Bernoulli observation and independent noise.
Published Theorem 2.2 on page 1974 gives a Frobenius online-SGD rate and Theorem 3.1 on page 1977 gives fixed-form asymptotic normality for scalar rewards from independent Gaussian matrix contexts.
Published Theorem 3.1 and equations (17)--(18) on page 2389 bound nearest-neighbor error for each unit-by-time counterfactual mean under an adaptive pooled sequential policy.

Published Theorem 2 and equation (14) on page 1724 give a Frobenius RMSE upper bound for nuclear-norm completion of an untreated potential-outcome matrix when adoption dates are independent across units conditional on the latent matrix.

Published Theorem 3 in Section 4 of article e70002 gives a restricted-strong-convexity and Frobenius-error guarantee for the low-rank term estimated by the weighted MAR objective in equations (2) and (11).
Published Propositions 1--3 develop tall-wide factor imputation rates and limit laws for missing common components, with average and individual treatment effects on the treated as applications.

The published COLT extended abstract on pages 3821--3822 and its public full version give entrywise consistency and asymptotic normality for synthetic nearest neighbors under causal missing-not-at-random sampling.

Published Theorem 5 on page 2021 compares Frobenius upper bounds for known-propensity IPW and uniform-risk nuclear-norm completion under independent Bernoulli observation with a low-rank probability matrix.
The published article and its public full version develop groupwise nuclear-norm completion and debiased asymptotic normality for fixed block or staggered missing-not-at-random causal panels.

Public Theorem 3.2 and Corollary 3.3 give a rowwise \(\ell_2\) treatment-effect-matrix upper bound for Algorithm 1, an armwise empirical-row-scaled SVD under independent Bernoulli assignments and low-rank arm means.
Published Theorem 3 and equation (10) on page 7 characterize variance improvement for a scalar adaptively normalized IPW estimator under independent treatment indicators.
Predictably weighted adaptive IPW scores yield scalar studentized martingale limits.
Balancing weights attain Frobenius guarantees and a lower bound under fixed heterogeneous missingness.
Debiased low-rank projection yields inference for a fixed linear form under independent sampling.

ArXiv Assumption 2 on pages 7--8 gives normalized third-moment, predictable-covariance, empirical-covariance, plug-in, growth, and variance-floor conditions under which Theorem 3.3 on page 8 validates simultaneous multiplier intervals for many martingale means.
Published Theorem 4 and equation (14) on page 348 validate a multiplier maximum for a coefficient matrix under modeled nonuniform missingness.

tldr: Under an explicit row-major global filtration, recorded propensities turn the effect score into a bounded matrix martingale, and the normalized maximum-row frontier is \(b_{nm}=1\wedge[(B\sqrt{nm}/\lambda_{nm})\sqrt{\log(en)}\,K r^{3/2}\mu q^{-1/2}\sqrt{n^{-1}+nm^{-2}}]\). IPW-SVD attains this rate under history-predictable assignments and a constant-propensity submodel gives the observed-data-measurable converse. Mehrotra et al. attain the same geometric rowwise matrix-error scale under independent assignments with low-rank arm means; the field-level advance here is the recorded-predictable effect-subspace frontier, weaker armwise structure, and matched converse. Athey et al.'s causal-panel completion and Sun et al.'s longitudinal MAR weighted completion target outcome imputation in Frobenius loss and neither imply nor are implied by this effect-subspace result. For the newly defined blind row-fraction SVD, a primitive oracle gap and propensity-path stability imply the random tangent gap; validity holds exactly when total drift \(\rho_{nm}\) is at most \(b_{nm}\), and the observed fit discrepancy \(\widehat\rho_{nm}\) diagnoses that boundary. A bounded-aspect rank-one \(0.25/0.75\) Markov sequence is a boundary example for this new blind procedure. Under a theorem-specific nonsaturation margin, leave-one-cell-out residuals yield simultaneous dense-query bands with a separate \(\sqrt{\log|\mathcal G_n|}\) cost.

project_justification.gap: Mehrotra et al. establish the geometric rowwise matrix-error scale for an armwise row-scaled SVD under independent Bernoulli assignments, but not an effect-subspace theorem under history-predictable assignment or a minimax converse over estimators observing recorded propensities. Cai et al.'s independent-entry subspace bounds, Han et al.'s online matrix-context regression, Dwivedi et al.'s adaptive nearest-neighbor arm-mean inference, Athey et al.'s causal-panel Frobenius completion, and Sun et al.'s longitudinal MAR weighted completion do not fill that joint gap. Khan and Ugander's scalar affine normalization does not analyze the new row-fraction SVD or supply an observed spectral drift diagnostic.
project_justification.niche: The field-level niche is a calibrated causal row-subspace frontier that separates predictable-assignment noise, oracle path distortion, empirical-denominator tangency, observable fit disagreement, and simultaneous-query entropy.
project_justification.fill: The project derives a maximum-row upper rate and measurable-estimator converse, proves the primitive-gap-to-tangent-gap transfer, calibrates the observable blind-versus-recorded discrepancy, gives an iff frontier and a bounded-aspect boundary example for the newly defined blind procedure, and derives Belloni--Oliveira increment and covariance conditions plus uniformly positive leave-one-cell-out studentizers for a direct-IPW multiplier band with a separate family-size factor.

related_work: Mehrotra, Tran, Vu, and Zampetakis are the closest rate comparator: public Algorithm 1, Theorem 3.2, and Corollary 3.3 in Section 3 give an armwise empirical-row-scaled SVD and the same geometric rowwise matrix-error scale under independent Bernoulli assignments, unknown propensities, and low-rankness of each arm mean. Their result informs the geometric term but does not allow treatment probabilities to depend on recorded history, does not permit high-rank arm means whose difference is low rank, does not target the effect matrix's left singular space, and gives no minimax converse. Cai, Li, Chi, Poor, and Chen impose independent Bernoulli entry sampling and independent noise in published Assumptions 1--2 on page 948; their diagonal-deleted Gram estimator has an \(\ell_{2,\infty}\) upper bound in Theorem 1, equations (16b)--(17) on page 950, and an independent-Gaussian minimax lower bound in Theorem 2, equation (22b) on page 953. ArXiv v5 pages 5, 7, and 10 corroborate those published locators; these results inform the perturbation and packing but do not cover a causal predictable IPW score. Athey, Bayati, Doudchenko, Imbens, and Khosravi define the untreated-potential-outcome completion problem on pages 1717--1718, impose independent noise and adoption dates in published Assumptions 1--2 on pages 1720 and 1724, and prove a nuclear-norm Frobenius RMSE bound in Theorem 2, equation (14), on page 1724. Their theorem does not imply the present result because it targets the control-outcome matrix and treatment effects on treated cells rather than the effect row subspace under within-unit predictable randomization; conversely, low rank of \(M=\mu^1-\mu^0\) does not imply low rank or estimability of their untreated matrix, so the present result gives neither their imputation bound nor their treatment-on-treated estimand. Sun, Zhu, and Dubin define the longitudinal outcome decomposition in published equation (1) and MAR propensity in Assumption 2 of Section 2, the weighted nuclear-norm objectives in equations (2) and (10)--(11) of Section 3, and the low-rank Frobenius bound in Theorem 3 of Section 4 of article e70002. Their result does not imply predictable-treatment effect-subspace recovery because its mask is MAR response missingness and its loss is Frobenius error for an outcome low-rank term; conversely, the present low-rank effect assumption supplies neither their covariate decomposition nor low-rank outcome term, and therefore does not imply their completion guarantee. Dwivedi, Tian, Tomkins, Klasnja, Murphy, and Shah use the exogenous factor model in published equation (4) on page 2383 and nearest neighbors for each unit-by-time counterfactual mean in Theorem 3.1 and equations (17)--(18) on page 2389; Assumption 6 on page 2397 and Theorem 4.1 on page 2398 delimit their Lipschitz factor class, which \(\mathrm{thm:dwivedi\mbox{-}separation}\) separates in both directions from the present model and target. The whole-neighborhood audit also covers Bai and Ng's published Propositions 1--3 for tall-wide factor imputation and treatment effects on treated cells, Agarwal, Dahleh, Shah, and Shen's COLT pages 3821--3822 and public full version for synthetic-nearest-neighbor entrywise causal completion under missing-not-at-random sampling, Choi and Yuan's published groupwise nuclear-norm and debiasing framework for fixed block or staggered missing-not-at-random panels, and Mao, Wong, and Chen's independent-Bernoulli low-rank missingness model and published Theorem 5 on page 2021 for Frobenius IPW completion. These adjacent results target missing outcome entries, averages, or full-matrix losses; none provides the recorded-predictable effect-subspace upper-and-lower frontier, while the present effect-only low-rank class does not imply their armwise, block-factor, or missingness-model assumptions. Han, Sun, and Zhang specify one scalar reward per independent Gaussian matrix context in published equation (1) on page 1964 and prove a Frobenius online-SGD rate in Theorem 2.2 on page 1974; Theorem 3.1 on page 1977 concerns fixed-form asymptotic normality. Tropp supplies bounded-increment matrix Freedman inequalities. Khan and Ugander's published Theorem 3 and equation (10) on page 7 analyze a scalar affine normalizer under independent treatment indicators, and their Discussion on page 18 identifies dependent indicators as an open extension; they do not define the row-fraction SVD here, so the Markov boundary example is not a refutation of their procedure. Hadad, Hirshberg, Zhan, Wager, and Athey justify recorded-propensity scalar martingale scores. Wang, Wong, Mao, and Chan provide a fixed heterogeneous-missingness Frobenius benchmark. Xia and Yuan's published Section 1 conditions after equation (5) require loading alignment and an \(\ell_1\) size condition for their independent noisy-matrix fixed-form inference; those conditions are not cited as support for the deterministic dense loadings here. Belloni and Oliveira's arXiv Assumption 2 on pages 7--8 states the normalized third-moment, predictable-covariance, empirical-covariance, plug-in, dimension-growth, and variance-floor hypotheses used by Theorem 3.3 on page 8; the multiplier-primitives lemma derives the non-covariance inputs and imposes their covariance stabilization directly. Ma, Niu, Zhang, and Zhu's published Theorem 4 and equation (14) on page 348 give a multiplier maximum for modeled nonadaptive missingness. Spruijt-Metz et al. make saved propensities and sensitivity to their omission concrete in HeartSteps II.

technical_internal_limitation: The corrected frontier is larger than \(b^0_{nm}\). With balanced dimensions and \(\lambda_{nm}\asymp B\sqrt{nm}\), maximum-row noise gives \(\sqrt{\log n/n}\), not \(n^{-1/2}\). At \(\lambda_{nm}\asymp B\sqrt{n\log n}\), normalized maximum-row loss can remain constant. The primitive class restricts only the effect matrix: the denominator derivative \(H^{\mathrm B}\) contains the separate arm means, and no primitive condition in this core supplies a frontier-rate estimator of those means from one realized arm per cell. Accordingly, the blind branch retains the implementable fit-disagreement certificate and does not assert a tangent correction. The simultaneous-band theorem excludes \(r=\min(n,m)\), because any rank \(r\) projection then interpolates the score and destroys residual studentization; this exclusion does not affect the rate, converse, or blind frontier. Sharp dependence on growing \(r\), \(\mu\), and \(K\) remains in the sharp-constant question.
honest_scope: Identification and the fixed-propensity algebra are reductions. Maximum-row martingale perturbation, the matched packing, the primitive-gap transfer, the ratio remainder, calibration of the observed discrepancy, Markov concentration, leave-one-cell-out covariance consistency, and multiplier approximation are to be established. Mehrotra et al. settle the analogous geometric rowwise matrix-error upper scale under independent assignments and armwise low rank; the open contribution here begins at predictable assignment, effect-subspace loss, effect-only low rank, and the matched converse. The blind row-fraction SVD is introduced in this core; the Markov sequence is its boundary example and makes no claim about a published procedure. Constant propensities make the oracle blind center equal \(M\) but do not erase the empirical-denominator tangent. The diagnostic is sharp only up to the \(b_{nm}\) stochastic resolution, so local alternatives inside that boundary are not distinguishable. No denominator-tangent correction is claimed because the existing primitives do not impose estimable structure on the separate arm means entering \(H^{\mathrm B}\). Cross-fitting is used only to construct residuals; its consistency follows from martingale concentration and low-rank approximation, not from an independence assertion. The sharp minimax constant is posed only along the explicit bounded-aspect path and only over estimators measurable from \(A\), \(Y\), and \(p\).

novelty_justification: Mehrotra et al. already provide the same geometric rowwise matrix-error scale for armwise row-scaled SVD under independent Bernoulli assignment, so that scale alone is not claimed as new. No located result gives the calibrated normalized maximum-row effect-subspace frontier under a recorded history-predictable unit-by-time mask, with only the effect matrix constrained to be low rank, together with a matching converse over observed-data-measurable estimators. Nor does a located result give the blind iff frontier whose latent total drift is recoverable to \(O_P(b_{nm})\) from observed disagreement between blind and recorded fits. Athey et al. and Sun et al. supply outcome-completion Frobenius results whose assumptions and conclusions do not imply this frontier in either direction; the wider audit of Bai and Ng, Agarwal et al., Choi and Yuan, Mao et al., and Wang et al. reaches the same target-and-experiment separation. Dwivedi et al.'s closest adaptive pooled result is formally non-representable in either direction. The Markov law is a boundary example for the new row-fraction SVD, not a claimed failure of prior normalization practice. No located matrix result combines this predictable effect-subspace frontier with a growing dense causal-query family while keeping query entropy separate from row recovery.

_pre_d0_cursor.topic: K1 prove IPW-SVD attains pointwise normalized max-row loss b_nm=K r^(3/2)mu q^(-1/2)sqrt(1/n+n/m^2) under recorded predictable masks. K2 match it by an adaptive-mask minimax lower bound. K3 prove blind row scaling is first-order valid iff restricted propensity drift rho<=b_nm. K4 keep b_nm separate and inflate simultaneous stochastic radii by sqrt(log |G_n|) for predeclared dense families |G_n|<=n^kappa. Include the rank-one .25/.75 Markov-mask witness and HeartSteps II consumer. PRESOLVE EVIDENCE REQUIRING VERIFICATION: Recorded propensities make IPW entry errors conditionally mean zero, so matrix Freedman concentration plus leave-one-row perturbation may recover the independent-mask rowwise scale. A constant-q subclass supplies a legal lower-bound packing. Expanding blind self-normalization should expose drift-correlated first-order bias. The Markov witness permits exact conditional calculations. Polynomial query families require a separate entropy multiplier; it cannot be hidden inside b_nm. Random denominator remainders and the iff threshold remain unchecked. A constant-propensity submodel also shows adaptivity cannot improve the minimax converse, but sharp constants remain open here. UNRESOLVED BOTTLENECK: Obtain martingale-sharp rowwise singular-vector perturbation, control adaptive self-normalized denominators, match the lower bound, and prove necessity and sufficiency of the drift threshold while separating simultaneous-query entropy. EARLY KILL TEST: Expand bias and variance exactly in the rank-one Markov witness. Stop if bias exceeds b_nm when rho<=b_nm, or if martingale concentration or sqrt(log |G_n|) inflation invalidates the stated pointwise benchmark.
